title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a computation in 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets' (manuscript p. 459, archive p. 317).

Setting. G is a group scheme of 2x2 matrices, apparently GL(2) over a base. ρ and σ are involutive operations on G. The scheme G*_{ρ,σ} parametrizes quadruples (α, β, μ, ε) satisfying the 'loop-type' equation α ρ(α)^{-1} = ε (β σ(β)^{-1}) ε_1(μ-1).

The objects involved are:
- B'_0, a Borel-type subgroup normalized so that it meets the centre trivially;
- A_ρ (equivalently T_ρ), the torus centralizing ρ;
- N'_σ, the part of the normalizer of the σ-torus on which ε_σ(b) = b^{-1} σ(b^{-1})^{-1} = ±1;
- E', a group in which μ = det u and the sign ε take values.

On the previous page Grothendieck proved that (u, a, b) ↦ (u a^{-1}, u b^{-1}, det u, ε_σ(b)) is an isomorphism B'_0 × A_ρ × N'_σ ≅ G*_{ρ,σ}. Injectivity there used T_ρ ∩ B'_0 = {1}, so u is recovered from α as the unique B'_0-factor of α modulo T_ρ.

This page passes to the projective group PG = PGL(2), where the scalars G_m are killed.

Question. When do two sections (u, a, b) and (u', a', b') have the same images α̃ and β̃ in PG?

Claim (27)-(28). This happens if and only if a' = λ_1 a and b' = λ_2 b with λ_1, λ_2 ∈ Γ(G_m).

Proof. The argument rests on four facts:
1. B'_0 → PG is a monomorphism.
2. A_ρ → PG and N'_σ → PG have kernel exactly G_m; call their images T̃_ρ and Ñ'_σ.
3. In PG one has T̃_ρ ∩ B̃'_0 = {1} (29).
4. Hence ũ and ã are uniquely determined by α̃ through α̃ = ũ ã^{-1}, and then b̃ is determined by β̃ = ũ b̃^{-1}.

Conclusion (30). There is an isomorphism
B̃'_0 × Ã_ρ × Ñ'_σ ≅ G̃*_{ρ,σ} ⊂ PG × PG × E',
(ũ, ã, b̃) ↦ (ũ ã^{-1}, ũ b̃^{-1}, δ(ũ)),
with δ(ũ) = det u (see the next page). This is the projectivized form of the explicit parametrization of the solution scheme of the twisted equation. It is a routine descent of the previous isomorphism modulo the central G_m × G_m action.
errors: Notation drifts between A_ρ and T_ρ (and between Ã_ρ and T̃_ρ). This is a consistency slip, not a mathematical error.

Two points used in (30) are left implicit. First, the sign ε = ε_σ(b) is invariant under b ↦ λb, since scalars are fixed by σ, so ε is recoverable from b̃; this is why it can be dropped. Second, the monomorphy of B'_0 → PG requires B'_0 ∩ G_m = {1}, which presumably follows from how B'_0 is normalized. Both points are correct but unstated.
Strictly, the necessity argument also gives u' = u. This is used implicitly but not stated in (28).

ideas.what: Explicit product decomposition (Borel-type part × torus × normalizer part) parametrizing the solution scheme of a twisted equation α ρ(α)^{-1} = ε β σ(β)^{-1} ε_1(μ-1) in GL2, then its descent to PGL2
ideas.modern_name: Explicit parametrization of a twisted-conjugacy / Lang-type solution scheme via a Bruhat/Iwasawa-type decomposition; passing to the quotient by the centre
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard linear algebraic group techniques (Borel, Chevalley, Lang)

ideas.what: Using the trivial intersection of the torus image with the Borel-part image (T̃_ρ ∩ B̃'_0 = 1) in PG to get uniqueness of the factorization
ideas.modern_name: Uniqueness in group factorization from trivial intersection of subgroups

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine technical step: the projective, mod-centre version of an explicit isomorphism established on the previous page. It is correct and contains no new idea beyond the computation within the larger, unpublished 'équation des lacets' project.
transcription_corrections: 'PG ≃ GP(A)' is uncertain in the image; it may read 'PG ≃ GP(1)' or similar notation for the projective group. The struck-out symbol before it looks like 'P̃G'.
In the middle of the page the image has 'Ã_ρ', but the parallel text uses T̃_ρ. Grothendieck mixes the two notations.
The '(27)' label in the margin refers to the equalities α̃ = α̃', β̃ = β̃' inserted in the question.
